pages.ko: 옛날 옛날 아주 먼 옛날에, 산 밑 작은 초가집에 부지런한 농부 부부가 살았어요. 밭은 손바닥만 하고 살림은 넉넉하지 않았지요. 그래도 무엇이든 생기면 이웃과 나누는 부부였답니다. "나누면 반이 아니라 곱절이지요!"
pages.t: Long, long ago, in a little thatched house at the foot of a mountain, there lived a hardworking farmer and his wife. Their field was no bigger than the palm of a hand, and they had very little of anything. Still, whenever they had something, they shared it with their neighbors. "Share it, and it isn't half — it's double!"

pages.ko: 봄이 오자 농부는 처마에 걸어 둔 씨오쟁이를 탈탈 털어 보았어요. 씨앗이 겨우 한 줌, 손바닥에 오도독 남았지요. "이걸로 온 밭을 어찌 채울까요?" 아내가 걱정했지만, 농부는 씩 웃으며 씨앗을 꼭 쥐었답니다.
pages.t: When spring came, the farmer took down the straw seed pouch that hung under the eaves and shook it out. Only one small handful of seeds rattled into his palm. "How will we ever fill the whole field with this?" his wife worried. But the farmer only smiled and closed his hand tight around the seeds.

pages.ko: 밭을 파던 농부의 괭이 끝이 쨍— 무언가에 부딪혔어요. 흙을 살살 걷어 내자 커다란 항아리가 쑥 나왔지요. 목에는 붉은 끈이 곱게 묶여 있었어요. "누가 여기 묻어 두었을까?" 부부는 낑낑 항아리를 마당으로 옮겼답니다.
pages.t: As the farmer was digging his field, the tip of his hoe struck something — clang! He brushed the dirt away gently, and up came a great big jar. A red cord was tied neatly around its neck. "Who could have buried it here?" The two of them huffed and puffed the jar over to their yard.

pages.ko: 마당을 쓸던 농부가 그만 됫박을 항아리 속에 톡 빠뜨렸어요. "어이쿠!" 팔을 쑥 넣어 건져 보니, 됫박이 하나, 둘, 셋… 항아리 가득! "하나 넣으면 가득! 또 하나 넣으면 가득!" 부부는 눈이 휘둥그레졌답니다.
pages.t: While sweeping the yard, the farmer accidentally dropped his wooden measuring box into the jar — plop! "Oh dear!" He reached in to fish it out and found one measuring box, and two, and three… the jar was full of them! "Put one in, and it's full! Put one more in, and it's full again!" The husband and wife stared with wide, wide eyes.

pages.ko: 이번엔 아까운 씨앗 한 줌을 살며시 넣어 보았어요. 스르르르— 항아리 속에서 씨앗이 소복소복 차올랐지요. "하나 넣으면 가득! 또 하나 넣으면 가득!" 손바닥만 하던 씨앗이 자루 하나가 되었답니다. 그해 봄, 밭에는 씨앗이 넉넉히 뿌려졌어요.
pages.t: Next they carefully put in their precious handful of seeds. Whoooosh — inside the jar the seeds rose up softly, higher and higher. "Put one in, and it's full! Put one more in, and it's full again!" That palmful of seeds became a whole big sackful. And that spring, the field was sown with plenty of seed.

pages.ko: 가을이 오자 밭에는 곡식이 넘실넘실 자랐어요. 농부는 체로 슬슬 티끌을 치고, 아내는 키로 까불까불 쭉정이를 날렸지요. 고른 알곡을 됫박으로 한 번만 떠 넣어도 항아리는 금세 그득! 곳간이 든든해졌답니다.
pages.t: When autumn came, the grain in the field grew thick and swaying. The farmer shook the dust out with his sieve, and his wife tossed the empty husks away with her winnowing basket. One single scoop of the clean grain into the jar, and it was brimming full in no time! Their storehouse grew nice and full.

pages.ko: 부부는 항아리를 혼자 쓰지 않았어요. 커다란 시루에 김이 모락모락 떡을 쪄서 집집마다 돌리고, 씨오쟁이마다 씨앗을 소복이 담아 이웃에게 나누어 주었지요. "한 줌을 나누면 온 마을이 배부르지요!" 마을에는 웃음소리가 가득했답니다.
pages.t: The couple did not keep the jar just for themselves. They steamed rice cakes in a great big earthenware steamer, all puffing with warm steam, and carried them round to every house, and they filled seed pouches to the brim and shared them with their neighbors. "Share one handful, and the whole village eats its fill!" The village was full of the sound of laughter.

pages.ko: 소문은 담을 넘고 고개를 넘었어요. 이웃 마을 욕심쟁이가 헐레벌떡 달려왔지요. "그 항아리, 나한테 파시오! 아니, 그냥 내가 가져가겠소!" 욕심쟁이는 대답도 듣지 않고 항아리를 덥석 끌어안았답니다.
pages.t: Word spread over the walls and over the hills. A greedy man from the next village came running, all out of breath. "That jar — sell it to me! No, never mind, I'll just take it!" And without waiting for an answer, the greedy man threw his arms around the jar and carried it off.

pages.ko: 욕심쟁이는 항아리를 제 마당에 떡 놓고 쌀가마를 통째로 밀어 넣었어요. "가득! 또 가득! 더 가득!" 쌀가마가 와르르 쏟아져 마당을 덮고, 담을 넘고, 대문까지 막아 버렸지요. 욕심쟁이는 쌀더미에 파묻혀 헉헉거렸답니다.
pages.t: The greedy man plunked the jar down in his own yard and shoved in whole sacks of rice. "Full! Full again! Fuller still!" Sacks of rice came tumbling out, covering the yard, spilling over the wall, blocking up the front gate. And the greedy man was buried in the rice pile, puffing and panting.

pages.ko: 소란을 듣고 욕심쟁이의 아버지 어르신이 달려왔어요. "얘야, 이제 그만하려무나!" 아버지는 항아리를 붙들고, 아들은 놓지 않고— 밀치락 당기락하던 그때, 어이쿠! 어르신이 항아리 속으로 폭 빠지고 말았어요. 다행히 폭신한 쌀 위였지요.
pages.t: The greedy man's father, an old gentleman, heard the fuss and came hurrying over. "Son, that's enough now!" The father held on to the jar, the son would not let go — and as they pushed and pulled this way and that, oh dear! the old man tumbled right into the jar. Luckily, he landed on soft rice.

pages.ko: 그런데 이게 웬일! 항아리에서 똑같은 어르신이 쑥, 또 쑥, 또 쑥 올라왔어요. 하나 둘 셋 넷 다섯… 똑같은 얼굴에 똑같은 흰 수염! "내가 진짜다!" "아니지, 내가 진짜지!" 어르신들은 저마다 수염을 쓸며 티격태격, 온 마을이 발칵 뒤집혔답니다. 그런데 항아리에서 나온 어르신들은 어쩐지 몸이 깃털처럼 가벼웠어요.
pages.t: But then — what in the world! Out of the jar rose another old gentleman just like him, and another, and another. One, two, three, four, five… the very same face, the very same white beard! "I'm the real one!" "No, no, I'm the real one!" The old gentlemen stroked their beards and squabbled away, and the whole village was turned upside down. But somehow, the old gentlemen who came out of the jar were as light as feathers.

pages.ko: 어르신들이 서로 밀치락달치락하는 바람에 항아리가 기우뚱— 쿵! 쩌억 갈라지자, 요술도 함께 풀렸어요. 깃털처럼 가볍던 어르신들은 팡, 팡, 팡! 비눗방울처럼 사라지고, 진짜 아버지 한 분만 남았지요. 욕심쟁이는 아버지를 와락 끌어안았답니다.
pages.t: As the old gentlemen pushed and shoved one another, the jar tipped over — thud! And when it cracked right open, the magic broke apart along with it. The old gentlemen who were light as feathers went pop, pop, pop! — vanishing like soap bubbles, until only the one real father was left. The greedy man threw his arms around his father and held him tight.

pages.ko: "아버지, 제가 욕심을 너무 부렸어요…." 욕심쟁이는 얼굴이 홍시처럼 빨개졌어요. 농부 부부는 깨진 항아리 조각을 툭툭 털며 방긋 웃었지요. "괜찮아요. 씨앗은 밭에 있고, 떡은 나누면 되니까요." 그날 온 마을은 커다란 시루에 떡을 쪄서 사이좋게 나누어 먹었답니다. 알맞게 가지고 나누면, 그게 바로 진짜 화수분이래요.
pages.t: "Father, I was far too greedy…." The greedy man's face went red as a ripe persimmon. The farmer and his wife brushed off the broken pieces of the jar and smiled brightly. "It's all right. The seeds are in the field, and rice cakes are for sharing." That day the whole village steamed rice cakes in a great big steamer and shared them all around. Having just enough, and sharing it — they say that is the true jar of plenty.
